basicMistakes.where: Operator surface has no buttons; the brief requires a live pause and resume of the countdown and neither is offered.

answer.reasons: Visually this is a clean full-frame holding card: a yellow top bar, a readable label, a very large clock, a yellow rule that doubles as a progress bar, and a sub-line, all well centred with generous padding. Long values wrap to two tidy lines without clipping (G-4, G-5, G-24, G-25), the empty state still reads sensibly, and the take and out are simple fades. It fails only on the operator side: the brief needs the countdown to be paused and resumed live, and the surface offers no buttons at all, so it cannot go on air as delivered.

A full-width navy holding band with a gold top rule, a centred label, a very large white timer and a thin gold progress bar beneath — exactly the plain, hall-readable look the brief asks for. The long label stays on one line inside the band at a slightly reduced size with no clipping (confirmed in the G-42 crop), empty values fall back to sensible defaults rather than a blank board, and nothing overlaps: the PAUSED tag sits clear of both the timer and the progress bar. Pause dims the timer and shows a gold PAUSED label; Resume restores it and the count continues (9:58 → 9:50 after resume), so both required operator actions are offered and visibly work. The Take and Out animate cleanly (band wipes, rule draws, content fades) with no stray furniture, and the progress bar's grey track remainder reads as designed rather than accidental.

otherProblems: With empty values (G-6/G-7) the name line still shows 'Alexandra Konstantopoulos-Vandermeulen' while the role line blanks, leaving the lower half of the panel empty; a hard-coded fallback name is a risk if an operator ever takes the graphic with no data, though it is not a brief case.
The blue accent bar is inset a few pixels from the panel's top and bottom edges rather than running full height; a viewer would not notice.
answer.reasons: A single dark panel with a slim blue accent bar, white bold name and a smaller light-grey uppercase role: calm, undecorated and exactly what an evening news desk would expect. The full long name and long role sit on one line each with even padding on both sides and top/bottom, nothing wraps, clips or escapes, and the white and grey text is clearly legible on the near-black plate over both the dark video and the light ground. Take and Out are a clean horizontal wipe with the text fading in after the plate; the Update frames hold steady with no jitter. Nothing a viewer would see keeps it off air.

otherProblems: Right-hand padding after the long name (G-4/G-24) is tight — the name ends about 35 px short of the panel edge — but it is contained, unwrapped and not clipped.
With empty values (G-6/G-7) the name field falls back to the long placeholder name while the role row collapses; harmless on air but an inconsistent fallback.
Mid-transition frames (G-11 Take at 300 ms, G-22 Out at 600 ms) show text masked at the panel's bottom edge as it slides in/out — this reads as a designed wipe, not a clipping fault.
answer.reasons: A plain dark-navy panel with a single light-blue accent bar, bold white name, thin rule and grey role: exactly the calm, undecorated register the brief asks for. The stress name and title sit on one line each inside the panel with no wrap, no ellipsis and no overflow on both the video and light grounds; contrast is strong everywhere and the rule sits clear of both lines. Take, Update and Out animate cleanly and settle to the same correct state. Nothing a viewer would notice as wrong.

basicMistakes.where: Operator surface offers no buttons at all; the brief's flag, clearFlag and final actions are not available.
No frame ever shows a goal flag for either side or a 'final' look; the board only ever shows the LIVE header and the score, so content the brief needs never appears.

otherProblems: Long team name wraps to four lines and breaks mid-word ('URHEILUSEU / RA') in G-4, G-5, G-8, G-9, G-22 and the f0 crop G-28 — reads as broken rather than designed; the two sides also end up with unequal space (four lines vs two).
During the Take at 300 ms (G-14) the 'LIVE' label is sliding in with its glyph tops masked by the panel edge — a brief but visible cut during the animation.
Empty-values frames (G-6, G-7) leave an unlabeled score box with blank name slots, which is acceptable only as a pre-fill state.
answer.reasons: The settled board itself is clean, readable and well-balanced — dark panel, green LIVE header, clear score boxes, good contrast on both grounds. But the brief's core live moments are absent: there are no operator buttons, so the goal flag can never be shown or cleared and the match can never be put into a 'final' look, and no frame shows either state. On top of that the long-name stress case breaks a word in half across lines, which a viewer would read as a mistake. A scoreboard that cannot mark a goal or a full-time result does not go on air.

otherProblems: Empty-values stress (G-6, G-7): the home cell falls back to 'HOME' but the away cell is left as a blank dark block, an inconsistent fallback that reads as an empty cell if an operator ever leaves a name unset.

Long home name (G-4, G-5, G-70) wraps to three right-aligned lines, leaving the left third of the home cell empty; it stays inside the panel and reads as justified-to-score, but the panel grows noticeably tall.
Full-time tab (G-40, G-41) is a little wider than the white score cell it hangs from; centred and tidy, but not flush with the cell edges.
answer.reasons: A compact navy three-cell scoreboard top-left, clean and legible on both dark and light grounds, with team names and scores at a comfortable TV size. Stress names wrap inside the panel rather than clipping, the goal flag drops a yellow 'GOAL HOME/AWAY' tab with a scorer underline that clears cleanly, full time swaps the score cell to white with a 'FULL TIME' tab, and resume restores the live look. Take and out are deliberate slide/fade reveals with no stray furniture. The operator surface covers flag (goalA/goalB), clearFlag and final; the only nits are an inconsistent empty-value fallback and minor tab proportions a viewer would not notice.

otherProblems: G-6/G-7 (empty values): the set-time pill beside OPENING STATEMENTS renders as a small empty outlined box; it should collapse when the field is blank.
G-8/G-10 (one side long): when only one name wraps to two lines the two clocks sit at different heights (one at ~850, the other at ~900), so the board's two sides no longer read as level.
G-4/G-5 (long values): the header stacks the round label and the pill on two lines and the panel grows taller; clean, but the panel top jumps noticeably between normal and long states.
answer.reasons: A clean, centred two-column debate clock: dark panel, gold accent marking the active speaker, large legible clocks, labels and names well spaced and balanced on both grounds. All three operator actions work on air — Switch moves the gold bar and starts the other clock while the first holds, Penalty drops ten seconds with a brief red flash and a -10 badge in the gutter, Reset returns both to 05:00 and pauses both. Long names and the long round label wrap inside their columns without clipping or collision; the take and out are tidy wipes. Remaining issues are small: an empty outlined pill when the set-time field is blank, and the clocks falling out of level when only one name wraps.

otherProblems: Penalty is never demonstrated: in G-24 to G-29 it is pressed from the post-Take idle state (no active speaker) and nothing changes, so the only evidence that the ten-second deduction works is absent from the frames.

After the Take nobody is active and neither clock counts (G-17); the operator must press Switch to start the first speaker, which is workable but means the brief's 'active speaker counting down' state does not exist until a second action.
Empty-values state (G-6/G-7) leaves an empty bordered badge next to DEBATE and a panel that is mostly furniture (dashes, divider) with nothing in it.

With the long name on the left (G-4/G-5, G-8/G-9) the second wrapped line of 'Government (Helsinki Model United Nations)' sits tight above the big 180; it does not touch, but the spacing is noticeably tighter than on the right side.
answer.reasons: A clean, balanced two-sided clock: dark panel with a gold rule, equal halves, readable role labels and large white seconds, and a clear active state (gold number, extended accent bar, dimmed opponent) that appears on Switch and counts down (180→179→171). Reset is shown to return both clocks to 180 and clear the active side, long values wrap or widen inside the panel without clipping or collisions, and the on/off transitions are standard wipes. Nothing in any frame is a basic mistake. The reservations are operational rather than visual: penalty was only pressed with no active speaker so it did nothing on screen, and the board sits idle after the Take until the first Switch; a director would still take this as delivered.

otherProblems: Empty-values state (G-6, G-7) leaves a large dark panel holding only the kicker and a stray rule line; an operator who takes it before data is loaded puts a near-empty box on air.
Long footer (G-4, G-5, G-27) is cut at a word boundary ('…VOTING IS') with no ellipsis, so the strap reads as an unfinished sentence rather than a deliberate truncation.
With the three-line stress question (G-4, G-5) the panel grows upward to y≈457, poking slightly above the frame's midline, though it stays left and leaves the right side clear.
Out transition (G-20) briefly shows the panel with empty bar tracks and percentages but no question; it is gone by 300 ms so a viewer would barely register it.
answer.reasons: A clean, well-structured vote board: dark panel with a single yellow accent bar, kicker, question, three to four option rows with bar tracks and right-aligned percentages, and a live-results strap, all on one left margin with a consistent grid. The leader is unmistakable (yellow bar, bold white label, larger yellow figure) while the rest sit in grey. The stress frames wrap the question and long options inside the panel with no clipping or collisions, the long kicker fits on one line, and the panel reads equally well over the dark studio plate and the light ground. The Take and Out animate in sensible stages and settle identically at 1.5 s and 10 s. The weaknesses — an empty-data panel that shows only the kicker, a footer truncated without an ellipsis, and a stress panel that nudges above the midline — are edge cases a viewer would rarely see and none of them break the graphic as delivered.

basicMistakes.where: After the Update to long options, the leading option label wraps to four lines inside a row that did not grow; its lines 'presenter would read in full' sit on top of 'A second long option that competes' in the row below, left column of the panel.
Same overlap still present at the settled 1500 ms Update frame: the first option's wrapped text collides with the second option's label; neither is readable.

otherProblems: With the long question (G-4/G-5, G-24) the question text shrinks to roughly 22 px, which is marginal for a television viewer; the settled long-value frames otherwise lay out cleanly.
The highlighted leading row's accent bar and brown highlight band extend slightly past the other rows' bar/percentage column, a small alignment nit.
answer.reasons: The settled design is clean and well balanced: a dark panel in the lower-left, the leading option highlighted in gold with a left accent, readable labels and percentages on both the video and light grounds, and the pre-rendered long-value frames (G-4/G-5) reflow to a taller panel correctly. But the live Update is what this brief is about, and when the options are updated to the long values on air (G-14 to G-18) the rows do not re-measure: the first option wraps to four lines in a single-line row and lands directly on the second option's label, leaving a text-over-text collision that is still there at 1500 ms. An operator updating options mid-show would put that on screen, so it cannot air as delivered.

A: Penalty never has any visible effect: A-24 to A-29 (Penalty after the Take) show both clocks still at 180 with no active side, so the ten-second deduction the brief requires is never shown in any frame; the Take itself (A-12..A-17) starts nobody, so Take+Penalty does nothing

With the brief's own sample values (A-2, A-3, A-16, A-22) no speaker name is shown at all — only the side labels PROPOSITION / OPPOSITION; the name line only appears in the long-value frames (A-4, A-8, A-10)
A-6/A-7 (empty values): an empty outlined badge box sits beside DEBATE holding nothing
A-4/A-5 and crop A-57: the two-line long name 'Government (Helsinki / Model United Nations)' sits very tight above the 180 digits; no overlap, but the leading looks cramped
B: B-6/B-7 (empty values): an empty outlined badge box sits beside OPENING STATEMENTS holding nothing
Clocks are shown as mm:ss (05:00) where the brief asked for seconds; a format choice a viewer reads fine but not literally the brief
B-24..B-28: the transient '-10' pill is placed on top of the centre divider line; it appears to have an opaque fill so the line does not run through the text, but it is a crowded spot for the badge

answer.reasons: Both are the same clean dark two-sided board with a title badge, side labels, big clocks and an active-side accent rule; neither has text collisions, clipping or legibility faults, and both carry the long stress values by wrapping inside the panel. B does everything the brief asks on the pictures alone: the Take starts the proposition clock (B-17 04:51), Switch moves the accent and count to the opposition (B-23 04:51), Penalty visibly takes ten seconds with a -10 flash (B-24..B-28 04:50 → 04:41), Reset returns both to 05:00, and the speakers' names are on the board with the sample values. A's Take starts nobody, so the Penalty step as delivered (A-24..A-29) changes nothing on screen and the brief's penalty is never demonstrated; its sample state also shows no speaker names. A is a tidy board but as delivered it does not show the penalty working, so I would put B on air.

A-25.jpg–A-29.jpg: the '-10' penalty pill is parked on top of the centre divider line; it reads as intended but is a slightly fussy placement

answer.reasons: A is a clean, balanced two-sided clock that does everything the brief asks on the pictures alone: names and clocks are large and legible, the active side is clearly flagged, the clock counts after the Take, Switch hands over and starts the other clock, Penalty shows a -10 badge and the clock drops to 04:50, Reset returns both to 05:00, long values wrap inside the panel and the panel grows to hold them. Its only blemish is an empty badge outline in the blank-field stress state. B is tidy and uses the same layout language, but with the brief's own values it never shows a speaker name, and when a name is supplied it is rendered as small print under the side label; worse, the Penalty step as captured changes nothing on screen, so the deduction the brief requires is never demonstrated. A airs as delivered; B would need fixes before it could.

B: Operator surface offers no buttons, but the brief needs pause and resume; no frame (B-8 to B-23) shows any paused state and the surface cannot produce one.
B-2/B-12/B-13: the heavy timer digits are tracked so tightly that the colon and the '4'/'5' crowd into each other — readable, but reads as crude rather than designed.
B-4/B-25: the long value of the subtitle line wraps to a second line with a single orphaned word 'starts'.
B-2 onward: the gold accent rule sits hard against the very top edge of the frame, where it reads as an accident rather than part of the composition.

answer.reasons: A is a clean, full-width navy band with a gold top rule, a one-line label that still fits at the long stress value (A-4, A-42), a large white timer readable from the back of a hall, a depleting gold progress bar, and a proper PAUSED state (A-14 to A-19) that resumes correctly (A-20 to A-25, A-36 to A-41); nothing overlaps, clips or spills in any frame, and the take and out are tidy. B is a full-screen holding slate whose text also fits and wraps cleanly, but its operator surface has no buttons at all, so the pause and resume the brief explicitly requires cannot be performed live — that alone keeps it off air, and its crude tight-set timer digits, orphaned wrap on the long subtitle and an accent rule jammed on the top frame edge are further marks against it. A airs; B does not; A is the clear choice.

A: Operator surface offers no buttons, but the brief needs pause and resume; no frame shows a paused state (basic mistake: missing operator action).
A-11.jpg and A-19.jpg: the take/out wipe masks the label, timer and sub-line mid-glyph (transition frames only, minor).

answer.reasons: A is a tidy full-frame dark holding look with a big readable timer and a label that wraps cleanly under stress, but it cannot be paused or resumed from the desk, which the brief explicitly needs, so it does not air as delivered. B is an opaque full-width band with a yellow top rule, a label that still fits on one line at its long value (B-42), a large white timer, and a progress rule; Pause greys the timer and adds a clear yellow PAUSED tag (B-14 to B-19), Resume restores it and the count continues (B-20 to B-25, B-36 to B-41), and it stays readable over the light plate (B-3, B-5, B-7). B is clean, balanced and does the job; it airs.

A: A-4.jpg / A-5.jpg: with the long question the panel grows upward to about y=457, nudging past the lower half the brief asks for (minor).
A-4.jpg / A-27.png: long footer stops at 'VOTING IS' with no ellipsis — looks clipped at a word boundary, not mid-glyph; a small nit.

B-4.jpg / B-5.jpg / B-24.png: the long question is shrunk to a single line of roughly 18–20 px text, too small for the main question on a television.

answer.reasons: A is a clean, well-padded dark board: kicker, question, four option rows with bars and a clearly dominant yellow leader, readable on both grounds; long values wrap and the panel grows to hold them, the Take/Out animate cleanly, and the Update swaps the kicker without disturbing anything. B looks designed at sample values, but once the operator updates the options to long labels the leading row does not grow and its label collides with the row below — a text-over-text basic mistake that persists in the settled frame — and its long question is squeezed to a size that would not read on air. A airs as delivered; B does not.

A: Text over text: A-14 through A-18 (Update of Options to long values) — the leading option's four-line label "A longer, more elaborate answer option the presenter would read in full" runs down over the second option's label "A second long option that competes"; the two labels are printed on top of each other and it is still like that in the settled frame A-18 at 1500 ms.

Empty-values frames B-6/B-7 leave a panel holding only the kicker and a bare rule (edge-case state an operator would not take).

answer.reasons: A is a tidy, well-proportioned poll panel in its static frames and even reflows correctly when loaded with long values up front (A-4), but the live Update the brief depends on breaks it: the rows keep their short-value heights and the leading option's wrapped label is printed straight over the second option's label (A-14 to A-18), still overlapping once settled. That is text over text on air, so A does not go out. B keeps its rows laid out under every value shown, carries the long question and long options by wrapping cleanly, marks the leader clearly in yellow, and its Take and Out are orderly. Its flaws are minor: the long-question stress frame creeps a little above the midline, and the post-update frame suggests a re-animation, neither of which a viewer would read as broken. B airs and is the one to take.

A: Role line is set fairly small and in a muted grey-blue (A-2, A-25); legible but secondary text is on the quiet side for a TV screen.
Right-hand padding after the long name is a little tight (~37 px to the panel edge in A-4) compared with the left margin.
Mid-Take frames (A-10, A-11) show the empty panel with its rule and then the role text rising through a mask — a designed reveal, not a fault, but it briefly reads as an empty box.
B: Role is set in small tracked capitals (~24 px cap height, B-2/B-25) — readable but at the lower limit of comfortable on a television.
Gap between the name's descenders and the capitals of the role is tight (B-25), though they do not touch.
Out animation (B-19) briefly leaves a blank dark panel with only the accent bar before it collapses — transient.

answer.reasons: Both are clean, calm one-panel lower thirds that carry the full 36-character name and the long role on a single line each, with no wrapping, no overflow and no clipping in the settled or stress frames; empty-role frames collapse the panel tidily in both. Neither has a basic mistake: the sliced text seen at 300–600 ms is a deliberate mask reveal, not a broken frame. B edges it for the brief: larger name, more generous and even padding inside a wider panel, and no rule — nothing decorative at all — which reads as the more authoritative evening-news card. A is equally airable but its rule and smaller, dimmer role line make it feel slightly busier and less bold.

answer.reasons: Both are clean, readable, calm news lower thirds: the very long name and role fit on one line inside each panel on both the video and the light grounds, no element crosses text, and the Take/Out animations settle cleanly. Neither has a basic mistake in a settled frame; the only clipping is momentary mask-reveal during transitions in both. A has bigger, bolder type, but its fixed-height panel leaves an empty band when the role is blank (A-6/A-7), which looks like a missing line. B sizes its panel to its content, keeps even padding, handles the empty state tidily, and its hairline divider is restrained enough for a public-broadcast look, so I would put B on air first, though A would also air as delivered.
